contentBlocks.text: Last week you learned S, M, A, and T, and even read the word 'sat'! Today, a new letter: P.

The letter P makes a quick popping sound: p, like at the start of 'pat' or 'pot'. Practice saying /p/ several times, feeling your lips pop apart each time. Now try blending it with letters you already know: /p/ /a/ /t/ — pat! You just read a brand-new word using a letter you only just met.
You just used a new letter to read a new word right away! Tomorrow we'll meet our second vowel.

objectives: Recognize and produce the /p/ sound for the letter P
Blend P with known letters to read the new word 'pat'
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review S, M, A, T and the word 'sat' from last week.
2. Introduce P and its popping sound.
3. Blend p-a-t together slowly, then faster, until it reads as 'pat'.
4. Move to the worksheet: trace P, then trace and blend 'pat'.
5. Close by comparing 'sat' and 'pat' — same ending sound, different first letter.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the /p/ sound in isolation before attempting the full blend
Ready for more: ask the child to think of another real word that starts with the /p/ sound
Comparing 'sat' and 'pat' reinforces that changing just the first sound changes the whole word — a genuinely useful phonics insight
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and blending activity — check that the child can produce the /p/ sound and successfully blend 'pat'.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: P is a high-utility consonant that, combined with last week's S/M/A/T, unlocks several new real CVC words — continuing the deliberate letter-sequencing strategy from week 1.

generationData.instructions: Trace each letter, say its sound out loud, then write it once more on your own.
